newsitem.title: USA: Carson Pirie November same store sales up.
newsitem.headline: Carson Pirie November same store sales up.

text.p: Carson Pirie Scott & Co said Thursday same store sales for the four weeks ended November 30 rose 4.1 percent.
Total sales for the month were $112.3 million, up 10.7 percent from $101.4 million a year ago.
Year-to-date same store sales rose 2.8 percent, while total sales were up 5.6 percent to $840.3 million from $795.4 million.
The 1995 year-to-date period excludes $25.0 million of sales from eight stores sold in March 1995.

"The November sales results provided an encouraging start to the 1996 holiday season," Stanton Bluestone, chairman, said in a statement. "We achieved our 10.7 percent sales gain through a solid 4.1 percent comparable store sales increase and an exceptional performance at our four new stores."
Men's and women's apparel, cosmetics, jewelry and textiles were the strongest businesses. Holiday-related merchandise sold particularly well throughout the chain, he added.

"We remain optimistic for the holiday season. Our customers have responded favorably to our merchandise assortments and we believe our new stores will continue to be strong contributors," Bluestone said.
